content:
lee: Hi team — first week here, quick Q: I have my okta + AWS role but I can't access Vault/KMS. Where do I request secrets access and who approves? Trying to get a DB password for local work.

maria: Welcome! :wave: For Vault/KMS we use the internal request flow. Start with the secrets request form: https://redwood.internal/ops/secrets-request (choose 'new-hire' and 'dev' environment). You'll need your manager as the approver.

lee: Thanks — is there any special policy name I should ask for? Also any short TTL/rotation basics I should be aware of so I don't mess with prod creds?

owen: Hey @lee — you should request the vault policy named `kv-read-redwood-dev` for read access to dev secrets. Never request prod DB creds unless your manager explicitly lists you as owner. Rotation basics: DB credentials in prod are rotated by the infra team every 30 days; dev secrets often have a 90d rotation but we prefer ephemeral creds. If you need short-lived AWS creds, request an STS token via the 'temporary-creds' checkbox on the form.

lee: Got it. What about KMS usage for encrypting local test blobs?

sasha: For KMS, request the 'dev-kms-encrypt' key policy on the same form. We log all KMS operations. If you're just testing locally, consider using the KMS mock in the devtools repo instead of hitting the real key. Link: https://git.redwood.dev/devtools/kms-mock

maria: Ops checklist for you: 1) submit form, 2) add manager as approver, 3) paste the secret path you need (e.g., `secret/data/redwood/service/x`), 4) request `read` scope only. We'll comment in the ticket when it's applied.

lee: If I already put in a form but it got stuck, who do I ping?

owen: Ping `secrets-ops` in #eng-security or DM me. I can escalate approvals if your manager is OOO. Also watch for `secrets-bot` messages — it posts when policies are attached.

secrets-bot: [automation] policy `kv-read-redwood-dev` attached to lee@example.com at 1802507010.

lee: Nice — I see the policy now, thanks. Quick CLI check: is this the command to read a secret?

maria: Yep, example: ```bash
vault login -method=oidc role=redwood-dev
vault kv get secret/data/redwood/service/x
```

lee: That worked. One more Q — if I accidentally commit a secret to a branch, what's the rollback/rotation process?

owen: If a secret leaks in git, file an incident via the internal security playbook immediately and mark the secret compromised. We'll rotate the key/credential and mark the secret version revoked. For dev creds we typically rotate and post the new secret to the same vault path. For DB creds we rotate the user password and update any infra configs.

sasha: Also run `git-secrets` locally (we have a repo hook) and use `git rev-list --objects --all` + `bfg` to scrub if needed. We can help with the scrub and rotation once you open the ticket.

lee: Awesome — that makes me feel better. Thanks everyone for the speedy help! :pray:

maria: Welcome aboard again — shout if anything else blocks you. :thumbsup:
